title: GitHub Pages for React

introduction.heading: Deploying a React App to GitHub Pages
introduction.description: A step-by-step recipe for publishing a React app to GitHub Pages using the gh-pages package. Follow the steps in order the first time you deploy a project; after that, step 5 (npm run deploy) is the only one you'll usually need to repeat.

prerequisites: A React project (Vite, or another build tool) already pushed to a GitHub repository
Push access to the GitHub repository you want to deploy to

steps.title: Install gh-pages
steps.description: Add the gh-pages package as a dev dependency. It handles pushing your built app to a gh-pages branch on GitHub.

steps.title: Set the base path for the sub-directory URL
steps.description: GitHub Pages serves your site from https://<username>.github.io/<repo-name>, so the build needs to know that sub-path to resolve assets correctly. In Vite, set base: '/<repo-name>/' in vite.config.js. In Create React App (now deprecated) you'd instead add a "homepage" field to package.json with the full URL.
steps.note: The trailing slash in base matters: '/react-gh-pages/', not '/react-gh-pages'. Replace it with your actual repository name.

steps.title: Add predeploy and deploy scripts
steps.description: predeploy builds the app automatically before every deploy, and deploy pushes the build output to the gh-pages branch. Point gh-pages -d at whatever folder your build produces.
steps.note: Use -d dist for a Vite project, or -d build for Create React App (react-scripts, now deprecated).

steps.title: Point the repo at GitHub
steps.description: If the local repository doesn't already have a remote configured, add one pointing at your GitHub repository. Skip this step if git remote -v already shows an origin.

steps.title: Build and Deploy
steps.description: Run the build and afterwards the deploy script. This triggers predeploy (a fresh production build), then gh-pages pushes that build to a gh-pages branch on GitHub, creating the branch if it doesn't exist yet.
steps.note: Run this again any time you want to publish a new version - it's the only step you'll normally repeat.

steps.title: Configure GitHub Pages
steps.description: Tell GitHub to actually serve the gh-pages branch as your site.
substeps: Navigate to the GitHub repository in your browser
Above the code browser, click the "Settings" tab
In the sidebar, under "Code and automation", click "Pages"
Under "Build and deployment", set Source to "Deploy from a branch"
Set Branch to gh-pages and the folder to / (root)
steps.note: After saving, GitHub will publish your site at the homepage URL from step 2 - it can take a minute or two the first time.

gettingStarted.heading: Quick Checklist
steps: Set base in vite.config.js (or "homepage" in package.json for CRA)
git remote add origin (only if not already set)
Set Pages source to the gh-pages branch in repo Settings
